elements.evidence: Section 4.1 permits either Party, including the Company as Customer, to terminate on notice without requiring cause.

elements.element: Customer may terminate on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires ninety (90) days' notice, not 30 days.

elements.element: Customer's termination notice must be written.
Upon Customer's termination for convenience, Customer receives a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
elements.evidence: No operative language requires HDI to refund unused prepaid fees on a pro-rata basis.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The clause grants either Party a termination right on 90 days' notice and does not restrict HDI's right to the end of a committed term.
The mutual termination provision permits the Company to terminate without a cause requirement.

elements.element: Customer's notice period is between 60 and 90 days.
elements.evidence: The clause requires ninety (90) days' notice, which is within the permitted 60–90 day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The added proviso caps the Termination Payment at the aggregate Section 3.1 payments relating to the three calendar months immediately preceding termination.
Section 4.1 grants the termination right to either Party, including HDI.

elements.element: Vendor may exercise its termination-for-convenience right only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The operative language does not require HDI's Termination Date to coincide with the end of the initial or a renewal term; the notice may specify another termination date.

elements.element: Vendor must provide 90 days' notice of termination for convenience.
elements.evidence: The mutual termination right requires ninety (90) days' written notice.

result.reason: The redline successfully caps the Customer's termination payment at three months of Section 3.1 payments and retains a 90-day Customer termination right, but it does not satisfy the fallback because HDI's convenience-termination right is not limited to the end of a term. It also lacks the preferred 30-day notice period and pro-rata prepaid-fee refund and continues to allow Vendor termination during a committed term. The breach and Section 1.6 fee carveouts are related but go beyond what was necessary for the stated fallback, while the required Vendor timing restriction was omitted.
